notes.Victor Wembanyama: San Antonio is without Dylan Harper (left hip soreness) and Tobias Harris (left calf strain), with Julian Champagnie expected to start in Harper's spot, so more of the offense runs through Wembanyama. He played 34 minutes Tuesday against Detroit, but the Spurs are 15.5-point favorites, so a lopsided game could trim his fourth quarter.
notes.Karl-Anthony Towns: Minnesota is without Anthony Edwards, Donte DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark, and Jonathan Kuminga is questionable, so the Wolves are thin around Rudy Gobert. Towns played 36 minutes Tuesday at Toronto with the offense built around him and Jalen Brunson, and a 1.5-point spread points to a close game and full minutes.
notes.Deni Avdija: Avdija is questionable after missing Tuesday's game at Minnesota, and Portland has also listed Toumani Camara as questionable. With Ja Morant and Shaedon Sharpe out, Avdija has been a main creator when he plays, so check his status before lock.
notes.Jalen Brunson: Brunson played 34 minutes Tuesday at Toronto, where the Knicks' offense ran through him and Karl-Anthony Towns. Minnesota is missing three guards and wings (Anthony Edwards, Donte DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark), and the 1.5-point spread points to a close game.
notes.Ty Jerome: Jerome has missed three straight games with right hip soreness, and Memphis had not filed its injury report Thursday morning, so his status is not posted. Cam Spencer has started in his place and led the Grizzlies with 26 points Wednesday at Cleveland.
notes.Charles Bassey: Bassey started Wednesday at Dallas with Al Horford out and played 22 minutes, his most in three games. Golden State is on the second night of a back-to-back and has not filed its injury report, and Horford and Draymond Green are both carried as questionable in our projections, so his start depends on that report.
notes.Trey Lyles: With Jonathan Kuminga out Tuesday, Lyles played 31 minutes off the bench while Cody Williams started and played only 13. Kuminga is questionable tonight, so Lyles' minutes ride on that call, and Minnesota is still without Anthony Edwards and Jaylen Clark.
notes.Will Richard: Richard played 27 minutes off the bench Wednesday, but a big part of his night came in garbage time of a 22-point loss at Dallas. Golden State is still without Stephen Curry, who is expected to miss at least another week, and its rotation has shifted from game to game.
notes.Jerami Grant: Grant has settled into a 20- to 23-minute bench role, playing 20 Wednesday at Cleveland. Ty Jerome has missed three straight and his status for tonight is not posted; if Jerome sits again, Grant's role has stayed the same in those games, so do not expect a jump.
notes.Luke Kornet: Kornet has been San Antonio's backup center at 13 to 16 minutes a night. With Dylan Harper and Tobias Harris out, the Spurs' bench is thin, and as 15.5-point favorites there is a path to extra minutes if the game gets away from the Clippers.
notes.Jaylen Wells: Wells has started every recent Memphis game and played 25 to 27 minutes in each, including 26 Wednesday at Cleveland. His role is steady, but Cam Spencer and Cedric Coward have taken the bigger shot share with Ty Jerome out.
notes.LJ Cryer: Cryer has started the last two Golden State games with Stephen Curry out, playing 24 minutes Monday and 19 on Wednesday, while De'Anthony Melton came off the bench. Golden State has not filed its injury report for the back-to-back at Memphis.

notes.Isaiah Jackson: Bradley Beal and Brandon Ingram are out for the Clippers. Jackson has been the backup center behind Brook Lopez at 15 to 19 minutes, but Yanic Konan Niederhauser is expected to make his season debut tonight and could take some of those minutes as he is eased in.
notes.Julian Champagnie: Champagnie is expected to start with Dylan Harper out (left hip soreness). He played 30 minutes off the bench Tuesday against Detroit, and Tobias Harris is also out.
notes.Cam Spencer: Spencer has started the last three Memphis games with Ty Jerome out and played 29 to 34 minutes in each, leading the Grizzlies with 26 points Wednesday at Cleveland. Jerome's status for tonight is not posted.
notes.Kyle Kuzma: Kuzma led Milwaukee with 30 minutes Wednesday at Miami, and the Bucks play again tonight on the second night of a back-to-back. Milwaukee trailed that game by 30 before a late run, and it has lost 11 straight.
